FA-C2.domain: analysis workflow: assessing disagreement in anonymous survey coding
FA-C2.epistemic_status: Synthetic workflow proposals only. No survey responses, coder scores, or measured agreement are supplied.

case.valued_outcome: Distinguish ambiguous category definitions from inconsistent application.
hard_constraints: Use the current response set only
Retain original coding decisions alongside any analysis
resources: Hypothetical anonymous responses and original category labels
Availability of independent coders is unknown
No access to respondents is supplied

raw_candidates.claim: Mapping disagreements to definition boundaries might identify ambiguity clusters.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Definition ambiguity predicts concentration near overlapping descriptions; application inconsistency predicts disagreement beyond those boundaries as well.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Disagreement well outside documented overlaps weakens the ambiguity-only account. A boundary cluster does not by itself exclude inconsistent application.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: inspect the current anonymous set and record boundary mappings beside preserved original labels.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Boundary interpretation may itself vary; neither account is established.

raw_candidates.claim: Independent recoding might reveal whether the same ambiguous cases repeatedly attract disagreement.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Recurring case-specific disagreements are predicted by category ambiguity more strongly than arbitrary isolated application mistakes.
raw_candidates.discriminator: The source offers a directional prediction, not a guaranteed advantage over boundary auditing. No recurrence weakens this prediction; unresolved coder independence defeats the comparison.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: establish independent coder availability, recode the existing anonymous set, and retain original decisions.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Independent coders are indispensable and unavailable status is unknown; no new response collection is assumed.
